long.title: 333 and 89: how New Zealand beat India by 244 runs (every ball analysed)
long.description:
New Zealand 333. India 89 all out. A 244-run defeat at Mount Maunganui. We took every ball of the 4th ODI (line, length, shot played, and whether the batter was in control) to work out who decided it and why: Matt Henry's triple-wicket first over, Will Young's 125 and the two lives that started it, and the middle overs where India lost the grip.

Sources: ball-by-ball data from ESPNcricinfo and Cricbuzz match pages (captured with our own tool, cross-checked over by over); result and Player of the Match from both. All numbers are computed by us from the ball data; 'not in control' is the Cricinfo shot-control flag. All graphics are original, not broadcast footage.

short.title: 0 for 3 after one over: India's chase in 6 balls #Shorts
short.description: The Replay Room: a ball-by-ball breakdown of NZ v India, 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui. Data: ESPNcricinfo and Cricbuzz match pages, analysis by The Third Man. Full video on the channel.

long.vo: Nought for three. After one over. That is how India's chase of three hundred and thirty-four began at Mount Maunganui. It finished at eighty-nine all out, a defeat by two hundred and forty-four runs. Here is exactly how it happened.

This is the Replay Room. We took every ball of the match: its line, its length, the shot that was played, and whether the batter was in control. Then we asked who decided it, and why. Two innings, two very different stories.

scene.teaser: Every ball · NZ v IND · 4th ODI

long.vo: New Zealand made three hundred and thirty-three, all out in the last over. India were bowled out for eighty-nine, in twenty-six point four overs. Matt Henry took the match award.

scene.title: Won by 244 runs.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: Start with the chase. This is every ball Matt Henry bowled. Thirty-four of his fifty-eight landed outside off stump, and half were short or back of a length. Nothing exotic. He asked India the same question again and again. And they kept getting it wrong.

scene.title: The same question, 58 times.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: Look at how India got out. Seven of the ten wickets fell to a defensive shot. Not a slog, not a mistimed pull. A forward defence. रोहित शर्मा and विराट कोहली were both out for nought, defending, in the very first over.

scene.title: Out defending.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: India scored off just one ball in four. New Zealand scored off more than one in two. India hit ten boundaries all innings, eight fours and two sixes. New Zealand hit forty-one, twenty-nine fours and twelve sixes. Almost two hundred runs in boundaries alone.

scene.title: Nothing to hit.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: Now the other half. New Zealand's innings, ten overs at a time. Seventy-two without loss in the powerplay. Then fifty-three for three. Then overs twenty-one to thirty: eighty-nine runs, and not a wicket. That's where India lost the grip.

scene.kicker: NEW ZEALAND · RUNS EVERY TEN OVERS
scene.title: The middle did it.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: And in the middle of it, Will Young. A hundred and twenty-five off a hundred and eight balls. He scored all around the wicket: twenty-seven runs from the cut, twenty-three from the cover drive, sixteen from the pull, twelve from the sweep.

scene.title: Every scoring shot.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: But it wasn't flawless. In his first fifty balls, Young was not in control on fifteen of them. Then from ball fifty-one to seventy-five, just twice. That's when he took over. Runs in each block: twenty-two, twenty-eight, thirty-five, and forty in the last thirty-three.

scene.title: Survive, then dominate.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: So how did he do it? He took the spinners and the quicker men on. Against कुलदीप यादव, a strike rate of a hundred and seventy-five. Against अर्शदीप सिंह and गुरनूर बराड़, a hundred and forty-five. But अक्षर पटेल kept him to sixteen off twenty-eight, and आक़िब नबी to twelve off seventeen. Those two got it right.

scene.kicker: YOUNG · STRIKE RATE AGAINST EACH BOWLER
scene.title: Who got it right.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: And he nearly wasn't there. In the second over, Young was put down twice, off consecutive balls, both off आक़िब नबी. The first was a regulation chance at slip, dropped by रोहित शर्मा. Young had made five. He went on to score a hundred and twenty more.

scene.title: In the second over.
scene.label: scored by Young after being dropped twice off consecutive balls, at five
scene.foot: Cricbuzz match commentary (dropped-catch events) · our own analysis

long.vo: So which of India's bowlers deserved more? अर्शदीप सिंह made Young and the others look uncomfortable, on a third of his balls, and took one wicket. आक़िब नबी, a quarter of his balls, four wickets. And कुलदीप यादव bowled eight overs for seventy-three, with nothing to show.

scene.kicker: INDIA'S BOWLERS · % OF BALLS BATTER NOT IN CONTROL
scene.title: Luck, and the lack of it.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: Then there was the start. Tim Seifert and Will Young put on seventy-two in the powerplay, without losing a wicket. Seifert hit fifty-eight off forty-eight. Finn Allen added forty-one off thirty. New Zealand never had to chase a start. India, after the same ten overs, were twenty-six for four.

scene.title: Seventy-two for none.
scene.foot: Ball-by-ball: ESPNcricinfo, Cricbuzz · 4th ODI, Mount Maunganui, 13 Nov 2026 · our own analysis

long.vo: So who decided it? In the chase, Matt Henry, in six balls. In the first innings, Will Young, but with help. Two dropped catches, a middle stretch of eighty-nine runs, and a plan of short lengths that India's bowlers couldn't turn into wickets.

There is one more number. विराट कोहली needed twenty-two runs, to become the first man to score two thousand ODI runs against New Zealand. He scored none. The fifth and final match is on the fifteenth of November. India lead the series, but they have two days to answer one question: can they leave the ball outside off stump?

scene.kicker: KOHLI V NEW ZEALAND · ODI RUNS
scene.title: Still 22 short.
scene.label: Two days to the decider
